Clauses from the Brightpath Hosting Master Services Agreement:

2.5 Unilateral changes. Provider may modify these terms at any time by posting the updated terms on its website.

response:
**Clause 2.5: Unilateral changes** (risk: high)
> Provider may modify these terms at any time by posting the updated terms on its website.

Why it matters: The provider can change prices, limits or liability without telling you or asking.
Suggested revision: Provider must give 30 days' written notice of changes; Customer may terminate without penalty before they take effect.

**Clause 5.4: Price increases** (risk: medium)
> Provider may increase fees at its discretion upon renewal.

Suggested revision: Increases capped at 5% per year (or CPI, if lower) with 60 days' notice.

**Clause 9.1: Limitation of liability** (risk: high)
> Provider's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer in the one (1) month preceding the claim.

Why it matters: One month of fees is far below the likely cost of data loss or a long outage.
Suggested revision: Cap at 12 months of fees, with no cap for data breaches, confidentiality breaches or gross negligence.

**Clause 11.3: Data on termination** (risk: medium)
> Upon termination, Provider may delete all Customer Data immediately.

Why it matters: You could lose your data before you have a chance to export it.
Suggested revision: Provider keeps Customer Data for 30 days after termination for export, then deletes it and confirms deletion in writing.

Overall risk rating: high.
